angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 591,345 km at 163.06 pc = 0.05 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 6.1327 +/- 0.0193 mas (same row, RUWE 0.89): 163.06 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.85 +/- 0.02 solar radii from Mortier et al. 2018, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of K2-263 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2018MNRAS.481.1839M/abstract): 591,345 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.88 +/- 0.03 solar masses from Mortier et al. 2018, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of K2-263 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2018MNRAS.481.1839M/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 5368 +/- 44 K from Mortier et al. 2018, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of K2-263 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2018MNRAS.481.1839M/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Mortier et al. 2018, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of K2-263 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2018MNRAS.481.1839M/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/k2-263.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.524, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, coloured from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
